identity.title: Improved Carbon and Nitrogen Isotopic Ratios for CH<SUB>3</SUB>CN in Titan's Atmosphere Using ALMA

paper_type_evidence.quote: To investigate Titan’s high-altitude nitrogen chemistry, we obtained observations using the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA) Band 6 receiver (211-275 GHz; $\sim$1.1-1.4 mm), in 2019 as part of project #2019.1.00783.S.

question.value: Measure CH3CN nitrogen and carbon isotopic ratios in Titan’s stratosphere to test nitrogen chemistry and fractionation.

evidence.quote: we measure the $^{14}$N/$^{15}$N and $^{12}$C/$^{13}$C isotopic ratios of acetonitrile (CH$_3$CN) in Titan’s stratosphere.
more accurate measurements of the CH$_3$CN isotopologues, in particular, are justified, to help test and improve models for Titan’s nitrogen chemistry.
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2019.1.00783.S.
Band 6 receiver (211-275 GHz; $\sim$1.1-1.4 mm)

evidence.quote: the first of which (Science Goal 1; SG1) covered the CO $J=2-1$ line

findings_qualitative.value: CH3CN is strongly enriched in 15N relative to atmospheric N2.

evidence.quote: We therefore show for the first time that $^{15}$N is strongly enhanced in CH$_3$CN compared to Titan’s main atmospheric nitrogen reservoir (N$_2$).

findings_qualitative.value: Measured Titan nitriles have consistent 15N enrichment, suggesting a common fractionated nitrogen reservoir.

evidence.quote: We find a consistent level of $^{15}$N enrichment within all Titan’s nitriles measured to-date, which implies they likely formed from a common, isotopically fractionated reservoir of atmospheric nitrogen.

findings_qualitative.value: Carbon isotope ratios agree with previous Titan and Solar System values.

evidence.quote: our $^{12}$C/$^{13}$C ratios are in good agreement with the values previously derived for Titan and various other Solar System bodies

findings_qualitative.value: The ~250 km abundance feature is needed to fit cores and wings, but its physical origin and latitude are uncertain.

findings_qualitative.value: Current data provide no strong evidence for nitrogen isotope variation with altitude.

claims.hypothesis: CH3CN is enriched in 15N relative to Titan’s bulk N2 reservoir.
claims.experiment: Retrieve disk-averaged CH3CN/CH3C(15)N from ALMA spectra and compare with Cassini N2 measurements.

evidence.quote: our CH$_3$CN/CH$_3$C$^{15}$N ratio of 68.9 $\pm$ 4.2 is significantly lower than the $^{14}$N/$^{15}$N ratio in N$_2$ of 167.7 $\pm$ 0.6 obtained by Cassini mass spectrometry ((cite: niemann_2010)), indicating strong $^{15}$N enrichment in Titan’s CH$_3$CN.

claims.hypothesis: CH3CN carbon isotope ratios agree with Titan’s other carbon-bearing molecules.
claims.experiment: Retrieve both singly 13C-substituted isotopologue ratios and compare with the literature mean.
claims.result: 89.2 ± 7.0 and 91.2 ± 6.0; both within 1σ of the Titan comparison mean.
claims.finding: Carbon fractionation is weaker than nitrogen fractionation.

evidence.quote: to our derived $^{12}$C/$^{13}$C ratios in CH$_3$CN of 89.2 $\pm$ 7.0 and 91.2 $\pm$ 6.0, we find that they are all consistently within a 1-$\sigma$ error margin.
We thus confirm the trend for a lower degree of isotopic fractionation in carbon than for nitrogen, across various Solar System bodies.

claims.hypothesis: The nitrogen isotope measurement can discriminate between photochemical models.
claims.experiment: Compare the retrieved ratio at ≈230 km with Vuitton and Dobrijevic–Loison model profiles.
claims.result: 69±4 agrees better with the Vuitton value ~55 than the Dobrijevic–Loison value ~120 with GCRs.
claims.finding: Vuitton gives better agreement, but the roles of cosmic rays and electrons remain uncertain.

evidence.quote: our value of $^{14}$N/$^{15}$N = 69$\pm$4 is in better agreement with the (cite: vuitton_2019) model value of $\sim$55 than the (cite: dobri_loison_2018) model value of $\sim$120
there is still room for improvement, so the precise importance of these processes should be revisited in future modeling efforts.

claims.experiment: Perform a continuously variable CH3C(15)N abundance retrieval and inspect ratio errors.
claims.result: SNR 16 is insufficient for useful altitude-dependent constraints.

referee_caveats_inferred: Uniform minor-isotopologue scaling makes the principal ratios conditional on a shared vertical profile shape.
A disk-averaged abundance feature can reflect unresolved spatial structure; it is not a uniquely localized vertical layer.
The 2017 wind field is applied to 2019 observations without a stated uncertainty test for temporal changes.
Discussion and spectroscopy appendix give inconsistent ratio revisions: nitrogen ~18% versus 20%, and CH3CN/CH3(13)CN ~34% versus 27%.
The Introduction and Discussion quote different second Gurwell HCN ratios: 72±9 versus 108±20.
Exact spectroscopic files and retrieval configurations are needed to audit the reported uncertainties and reproduce the final ratios.
